title: Coherent reduction preserves independent-coefficient K-flatness
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. Write $L^0_W=\lim\circ U_W$ and $r_W=\operatorname{leftAdjoint}(L^0_W)$ for ordinary coherent reduction, equipped with its specified adjunction $r_W\dashv L^0_W$ and unit $\eta^0_W$; concretely its components are quotient extension $B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}M$ and its transitions are induced by the actual quotient maps. A superscript $c$ means termwise application to cochain complexes. For a coherent complex $C$, let $\lambda_C:q_W((L^0_W)^c C)\to\mathcal L_W(q^s_WC)$ be the canonical right-derived limit unit, with the exact-restriction/localization factorization inserted (the map named pullbackTensorLimitUnit). For every good integral complex $P$, $r_W^cP$ is K-flat as a complex of module sheaves on the actual ringed sequence site. Explicitly, for every acyclic complex $Z$ of sequence modules,
$$\operatorname{Tot}(Z\otimes r_W^cP)\text{ is acyclic}.$$
The predicate is IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients with sequence-site object universe $u+1$, morphism universe $u$ and module universe $u+1$; it quantifies over all such acyclic $Z$, not just levelwise normalized systems. This is pullbackTensorReductionGood. The input has flat terms because it is good; no extra termwise-flatness condition is imposed on any test complex or any output datum.

proof.text: For every n use pullbackTensorReductionEvaluationComplex to identify evaluation of the ordinary reduction of P with scalarReductionExtension applied degreewise to P. The first clause of coefficientTensorModelPreservation preserves K-flatness under this scalar extension for every K-flat P, with no flatness assumption on the quotient ring. Transport along the stated cochain isomorphism. In particular it applies to P.property.1 for each good P.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YN, 07A4 and 0941; assembly of the existing Lean declarations named in this step.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary acyclic sequence complex Z. Exact evaluation gives an acyclic complex Z_n for every n. The uniquely specified coefficientEvaluationTensorIso identifies evaluation of Tot(Z tensor rP) with Tot(Z_n tensor (rP)_n). K-flatness from the first step makes the latter acyclic. The componentwise-exactness field of semilinearDerivedSections.systems, applied to each short complex of Tot(Z tensor rP), then gives acyclicity of the sequence complex itself. This tests every Z in coefficient universe u+1, so proves precisely IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients at the displayed universes. No condition on Z or on its horizontal transitions is imposed.
